summary: This JUnit test class checks two behaviours of the Thermostat: that a cold room in normal mode reports "Heating", and that the same-ish temperature in eco mode is allowed to stay "Idle" because eco mode tolerates cooler rooms before turning on the heat.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is how you mark a method as a test the test runner should execute.
A static import lets you write assertEquals(...) directly instead of Assertions.assertEquals(...), keeping the tests short and readable.
Every method carrying this annotation is discovered and run automatically; without it, the method would simply be ignored.
The method name states the expected behaviour in plain words, so a failure report tells you what broke without reading the body.
Arranges the test: a 60-degree room with eco mode switched off, which is well below the normal comfort threshold.
The expected value comes first and the actual value second; if they differ, JUnit fails the test and shows both.
The new test added in this exercise, aimed at the one behaviour eco mode introduces rather than at the thermostat as a whole.
Passing true turns eco mode on, which lowers the temperature at which heating kicks in.
At 66 degrees a normal thermostat would heat, so expecting "Idle" here proves eco mode really did shift the threshold down.
